log.limits: Primary list is the Office of Federal Acknowledgment List of Petitioners by State dated 2013-11-12 (the newest list bia.gov still posts). The fetch tool cut its text at about 73,800 characters, partway into Vermont, so Vermont, Virginia, Washington, West Virginia and Wisconsin come from the 2008-09-22 edition (University of North Texas End of Term 2008 archive, captured 2009-05-08). Any letters of intent filed in those states between 2008 and 2013 are missing; petition numbers 319 and 338 were not found anywhere (323 is the Pamunkey Indian Tribe). No Wyoming section exists in the 2008 edition. Rows were extracted by a summarizing fetch tool rather than from the raw PDF, because bia.gov blocks curl and web.archive.org was unreachable from this session (both curl and the fetch tool). Names, dates and Federal Register citations taken only from the lists (mostly pre-1994 determinations) carry medium confidence and should be spot-checked. Determinations from 1994 on were checked against Federal Register API metadata. Groups with only a letter of intent that are not on the current Petitions in Process list are typed unrecognized (inactive); bia.gov says groups on the 2013 list may no longer be active petitioners under the current (2015) regulations, which dropped letters of intent. Canoncito Band of Navajos (#114) got no entity because it is part of the roster Navajo Nation. Federation: Moorish Science Temple of America (#167) is included as listed, though the Department found it ineligible to petition. Groups whose older letter-of-intent number matches a current 400-series petition were merged when the names are identical (#140 to #411, #139 to #406, #239 to #401, #158 to #403) and for Mattaponi (#157 to #408), where the names are close and the match is noted. Amah Mutsun Band of Ohlone/Costanoan Indians (#120) and Amah Mutsun Tribal Band of Mission San Juan Bautista (#412) are kept as separate entities because the names differ. Two different groups share #336 on the 2013 list. No official websites were recorded, because none was clearly identifiable from these sources and searching each group one by one was out of scope. No state-recognition facts were recorded. No Native Hawaiian groups appear in any petitioner list read. State-presence facts record only the state the Office of Federal Acknowledgment lists, coded presence "other".
log.narrative: Read the agent contract and roster. Found the 2013 petitioner list and current status pages on bia.gov through web search, then read them with the web-fetch tool. bia.gov refused curl and the Wayback Machine was blocked, so no Wayback snapshot was used; every bia.gov page is the live copy read 2026-11-21. The 2013 PDF was extracted state by state. Its last states were cut off, so the 2008 edition from the University of North Texas archive filled them in, and the 2013 status summary supplied Washington determination dates. Pulled every Bureau of Indian Affairs Federal Register document matching acknowledgment terms through the API (190 documents) and linked proposed findings, final determinations, reconsiderations, receipt notices for the 400-series petitions, and re-petition notices to petition numbers. Built: entities for non-roster petitioners; recognition facts (petitioning for the 22 current petitions and the 3 re-petition requests; unrecognized for denied, withdrawn, ineligible and inactive letter-of-intent groups); federal recognition facts on 41 roster petition entries (Part 83 acknowledgments with final-determination citations, plus legislative and administrative recognitions, including the 2018 Virginia act, the 2019 Little Shell act and the 2025 Lumbee act); state-presence facts; and former and alternate names parsed from the list parentheticals. Diacritics such as Fernandeño and Juaneño are kept in UTF-8 names; only ids are ASCII.
